procedure.description: periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal

denial.carcText: Payment adjusted because the payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 19371 (periprosthetic capsulectomy, breast, with implant removal) with date of service 2026-07-14. CARC 151: Payment adjusted because the payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: A revision procedure on the same breast was paid within the prior six years; the documentation does not support an additional procedure.

criteria.text: Baker grade III or IV capsular contracture with pain or deformity, or implant rupture confirmed by imaging.
The original implants were placed for reconstruction after mastectomy, for a congenital deformity, or for another covered medical indication.
Symptoms documented for at least 3 months.

chart.text: From the referring physician: please evaluate for surgical management. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

38 year old woman here about her implants. Discussed capsulectomy with implant removal and the options for replacement versus leaving them out. Her history otherwise: mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year, reflux on omeprazole as needed. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Quit smoking 12 years ago, no alcohol, works two jobs. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Right breast is hard as a rock, distorted upward, tender to the touch, I would grade it Baker IV. Left is a Baker III, firm but not painful. Implants were placed in 2020 as part of her reconstruction after a right mastectomy for cancer, left side for symmetry. The hardening on the right started about 6 months ago and has gotten steadily worse, now hurts to lie on that side.
Blood pressure check. 120 over 85 today, 121 over 85 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 12 weeks.
MRI breast implants: right implant with a linguine sign consistent with intracapsular rupture, thickened capsule. Left implant intact with a thickened capsule and no rupture.
Back to go over the MRI and the plan. She wants the right one out and both capsules addressed. Vitals today 119 over 89, pulse 78.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Twisted the left ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Vitamin D came back 21. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Mole on the left forearm that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Pre-op. Consent signed for bilateral capsulectomy with implant removal, right side en bloc if the capsule allows. Labs fine.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 151 denial can be answered from the record.
